statement: The Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye.
explanation: Too narrow. Even Chinese astronaut Yang Liwei confirmed he couldn't see it.

statement: A human could survive on Mars without a spacesuit for about 2 minutes.
explanation: You'd lose consciousness in ~15 seconds due to lack of oxygen. Death follows in minutes from hypoxia and rapid decompression.

statement: Sharks are the ocean's top predators and have no natural enemies.
explanation: Orcas (killer whales) regularly hunt and kill great white sharks, flipping them onto their backs to cause tonic immobility.

statement: The human body generates enough heat in 30 minutes to boil half a litre of water.
explanation: The human body produces about 100 watts of heat at rest — enough to boil 0.5L of water in around 30 minutes.

statement: Diamonds are the hardest natural substance on Earth.
explanation: Diamonds score 10 on the Mohs hardness scale — the maximum. Only synthetic materials like wurtzite boron nitride are harder.

statement: You lose most of your body heat through your head.
explanation: The head accounts for only about 10% of heat loss — proportional to its surface area. The myth came from a flawed 1950s military study.

statement: Goldfish have a 3-second memory.
explanation: Studies show goldfish remember learned behaviours for months. They can be trained to press levers and navigate mazes.

statement: The tongue is the strongest muscle in the human body.
explanation: The masseter (jaw) is strongest relative to size; the glutes and quads produce more raw force. The tongue myth has no scientific basis.
hook: Is your tongue your strongest muscle?

statement: Water drains clockwise in the southern hemisphere and anticlockwise in the north.
explanation: The Coriolis effect is real but too weak to affect a bathtub. Drain direction is determined by the bowl's shape and residual motion.

statement: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
explanation: The Empire State Building is struck ~23 times per year. Tall structures are natural lightning rods and attract repeated strikes.

statement: Humans are the only animals that cry from emotion.
explanation: Elephants, chimpanzees and dogs produce tears in emotional states. Whether it's 'crying' emotionally is still debated by scientists.

statement: If you shave hair, it grows back thicker and darker.
explanation: Shaving cuts hair at its widest point, making regrowth feel stubbly and appear darker — but it doesn't change growth rate or colour.

statement: Eating carrots improves your night vision.
explanation: British WWII propaganda invented this to hide radar technology. Carrots help if you're deficient in vitamin A — otherwise they do nothing.

statement: The sun is yellow.
explanation: The Sun emits white light. It appears yellow or orange from Earth's surface due to atmospheric scattering. From space it is white.

statement: Bats are blind.
explanation: All bat species can see. Most use echolocation to navigate in the dark, but their eyes function — some bats have excellent vision.

statement: The human body replaces all its cells every 7 years.
explanation: Different cells have different lifespans. Neurons can last a lifetime; gut cells last 5 days. There's no uniform 7-year cycle.
hook: Do you replace yourself every 7 years?

statement: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain on Earth.
explanation: Everest is highest above sea level (8,848m). Mauna Kea (Hawaii) is tallest from base to peak (10,210m). Chimborazo (Ecuador) is furthest from Earth's centre.

statement: Napoleon was extremely short for his time.
explanation: Napoleon stood 5'7" — average for a Frenchman in the 1800s. The 'short Napoleon' myth came from British propaganda and a unit conversion error.

statement: Humans have only 5 senses.
explanation: We have at least 9: sight, hearing, taste, smell, touch, proprioception, thermoception, nociception, and equilibrioception. Aristotle only counted 5.
hook: How many senses do humans have?

statement: Chewing gum stays in your stomach for 7 years if swallowed.
explanation: Gum base is indigestible but still passes through the digestive system in days, like other insoluble fibre.

statement: Bulls are enraged by the colour red.
explanation: Cattle are red-green colour-blind. It's the movement of the matador's cape that provokes bulls — not the colour.

statement: We only use 10% of our brain.
explanation: Brain imaging shows all regions are active. Even during sleep, most of the brain has some activity. The 10% myth is completely fabricated.

statement: Hot water freezes faster than cold water.
explanation: This is the Mpemba Effect, documented since Aristotle. Under specific conditions, hot water can freeze faster than cold. The mechanism is still debated.

statement: The Great Wall of China is a single continuous wall.
explanation: The 'Wall' is a series of walls, trenches, and natural barriers built across different dynasties. Large gaps exist, especially in the west.

statement: Humans and dinosaurs coexisted on Earth.
explanation: Non-avian dinosaurs went extinct ~66 million years ago. Modern humans appeared ~300,000 years ago. There's a 65.7 million-year gap.

statement: Antibiotics are effective against viral infections like the flu.
explanation: Antibiotics kill bacteria. Viruses like influenza are unaffected by them. Overuse of antibiotics contributes to antibiotic resistance.

statement: The Amazon River discharges more water than any other river on Earth.
explanation: The Amazon discharges about 20% of all freshwater entering the world's oceans — more than the next 7 largest rivers combined.

statement: You can see stars during the day from the bottom of a deep well.
explanation: This ancient belief has been tested and disproved. Daylight scattering in the atmosphere is too bright, even in a narrow column.

statement: The Moon has its own light.
explanation: The Moon produces no light. It reflects sunlight. The Sun generates light; the Moon is just a very large mirror.

statement: A penny dropped from the Empire State Building could kill someone.
explanation: A penny is too light and aerodynamic. It reaches terminal velocity of ~30km/h — enough to sting but not penetrate skin, let alone kill.

statement: The Amazon Rainforest produces 20% of the world's oxygen.
explanation: The Amazon produces AND consumes oxygen in roughly equal measure. It's essentially carbon-neutral. The '20% of oxygen' figure is a widespread misstatement.

statement: Humans swallow an average of 8 spiders a year in their sleep.
explanation: This is completely fabricated. Spiders avoid vibrations and CO₂ — sleeping humans are exactly what they avoid.

statement: Glass is technically a liquid that flows very slowly over centuries.
explanation: Medieval glass is thicker at the bottom because it was made unevenly, not because it flowed. Modern science classifies glass as an amorphous solid.

statement: The human eye can see a candle flame from 48km (30 miles) away in darkness.
explanation: On a dark, clear night with no obstructions, the human eye can theoretically detect a single candle flame at ~48km.
hook: How far can you really see?

statement: Sugar makes children hyperactive.
explanation: Multiple double-blind studies have found no link between sugar and hyperactivity in children. It's parental expectation, not physiology.

statement: Einstein failed his university entrance exam.
explanation: Einstein failed the non-science sections (French, botany) of the ETH entrance exam in 1895, but excelled in maths and physics. He retook it and passed.

statement: The Eiffel Tower grows taller in summer.
explanation: The iron structure expands in heat — the Eiffel Tower can be up to 15cm taller in summer than in winter due to thermal expansion.

statement: Humans are the only animals that have sex for pleasure.
explanation: Bonobos, dolphins, and several other animals have been observed engaging in sexual behaviour beyond reproduction — including for social bonding.

statement: Chameleons change colour to match their background.
explanation: Chameleons primarily change colour to communicate — expressing mood, temperature regulation, and mating signals. Camouflage is secondary.

statement: There is no gravity in space.
explanation: Gravity exists everywhere in space. Astronauts feel weightless because they're in free fall around Earth — not because gravity is absent.

statement: Alcohol warms you up.
explanation: Alcohol causes blood vessels to dilate, making you feel warmer while actually accelerating heat loss. It lowers core body temperature.

statement: Humans are descended from chimpanzees.
explanation: Humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor that went extinct ~6-8 million years ago. We evolved in parallel, not from each other.

statement: You should wake a sleepwalker immediately for their safety.
explanation: Waking a sleepwalker is not dangerous to you — but it can cause confusion or distress for them. It's better to gently guide them back to bed.

statement: Oxygen is the most abundant gas in Earth's atmosphere.
explanation: Nitrogen makes up 78% of Earth's atmosphere. Oxygen is second at 21%. Argon (0.93%) comes third.

statement: Humans are the slowest runners in the animal kingdom.
explanation: Humans are among the best long-distance runners on Earth. We can outrun horses over marathon distances. Short-term we're slow; endurance-wise, we're exceptional.

statement: Tomatoes are vegetables.
explanation: Botanically, tomatoes are fruits (they contain seeds and develop from a flower). Legally and culinarily, they're vegetables. The US Supreme Court agreed in 1893.

statement: You should drink 8 glasses of water a day.
explanation: The 8-glass rule has no scientific basis. Hydration needs vary by body size, activity, and climate. Most people don't need exactly 8 glasses.

statement: The sun rises in the east and sets in the west every day.
explanation: The Sun rises exactly due east and sets due west only twice a year (the equinoxes). Otherwise it varies significantly by season and latitude.
hook: Does the sun rise in the east?

statement: Elephants are afraid of mice.
explanation: This ancient myth was debunked by experiments. Elephants don't single out mice. They can be startled by any small unfamiliar moving object.

statement: The North Star is the brightest star in the night sky.
explanation: Polaris (the North Star) is only the 48th brightest star. Sirius is the brightest star visible from Earth. Jupiter and Venus outshine them both.

statement: Napoleon was exiled to Elba for the rest of his life.
explanation: Napoleon escaped Elba after just 300 days, returned to power for the Hundred Days, and was only permanently exiled to Saint Helena after Waterloo.

statement: Cats always land on their feet.
explanation: Cats have a 'righting reflex' and usually land on their feet from moderate heights. Falls from very low or very high heights can still injure them.

statement: Swimming after eating causes cramps and drowning.
explanation: While intense exercise after a large meal may cause mild discomfort, there is no evidence that swimming after eating causes cramps or drowning.

statement: The human body has 206 bones.
explanation: Adult humans have exactly 206 bones. Babies are born with 270–300 bones; many fuse as we grow.

statement: Sushi means 'raw fish'.
explanation: Sushi means 'sour rice' (vinegared rice). The term refers to the rice, not the topping. Sashimi is specifically sliced raw fish.
hook: Do you know what sushi means?

statement: A group of crows is called a murder.
explanation: The collective noun for crows is indeed a 'murder'. Other notable examples: a parliament of owls, an unkindness of ravens.
hook: What's a group of crows called?

statement: The Sahara Desert is the world's largest desert.
explanation: Antarctica is the world's largest desert. A desert is defined by low precipitation, not heat. Antarctica receives less rainfall than the Sahara.

statement: Rome was built in a day.
explanation: The Roman Empire took roughly 244 years to reach its greatest extent under Trajan in 117 CE. The saying is proverbial, not historical.
hook: Was Rome built in a day?

statement: All continents were once joined as one landmass.
explanation: The supercontinent Pangaea existed ~335–175 million years ago. Continental drift slowly separated it into the continents we know today.

statement: The word 'set' has the most definitions in the English language.
explanation: 'Set' has over 430 definitions in the Oxford English Dictionary — the most of any English word.
hook: What word has the most meanings?

statement: Sharks are the only fish that can blink with both eyes.
explanation: Sharks don't actually have eyelids in the traditional sense. Some species have a nictitating membrane but can't 'blink' both eyes.

statement: A group of crows is called a murder.
explanation: A gathering of crows is indeed called a murder of crows, a collective noun dating back centuries.

statement: Elephants are the only animals that cannot jump.
explanation: Hippos and sloths also cannot jump. Elephants are notable but not the only ones.

statement: Butterflies taste with their feet.
explanation: Butterflies have taste sensors on their feet, allowing them to taste what they land on.

statement: A cow can walk upstairs but not downstairs.
explanation: The structure of a cow's knees makes it easy to go up stairs but very difficult to go down.

statement: Penguins mate for life.
explanation: Most penguin species are socially monogamous within a season, but many switch partners between breeding seasons.

statement: A snail can sleep for 3 years.
explanation: Snails can hibernate or estivate (summer sleep) for up to 3 years when conditions are too dry.

statement: Goldfish have a memory span of only 3 seconds.
explanation: Goldfish actually have a memory of several months. The 3-second myth has been debunked by researchers.
hook: Goldfish are smarter than you think!

statement: Dolphins sleep with one eye open.
explanation: Dolphins practice unihemispheric sleep — one half of their brain rests while the other stays alert.

statement: Flamingos are born pink.
explanation: Flamingo chicks are born white or gray. They turn pink from carotenoid pigments in the algae and shrimp they eat.

statement: A group of owls is called a parliament.
explanation: Owls gathered together are collectively known as a parliament, reflecting their wise reputation.

statement: Sea otters hold hands while sleeping.
explanation: Sea otters hold hands (or wrap in kelp) while sleeping to avoid drifting apart from their group.

statement: All polar bears are left-handed.
explanation: This is a popular myth. No scientific evidence supports that polar bears are predominantly left-pawed.

statement: Octopuses have three hearts.
explanation: Octopuses have three hearts: two branchial hearts pump blood through the gills, one systemic heart pumps it through the body.

statement: Cats always land on their feet.
explanation: Cats have a righting reflex but don't always land safely — especially from very short falls before the reflex activates.

statement: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
explanation: Lightning absolutely can and does strike the same place multiple times. The Empire State Building is struck about 23 times per year.

statement: Humans share 50% of their DNA with bananas.
explanation: Humans and bananas share about 50% of their DNA because many basic genetic functions are the same across all life.

statement: Hot water freezes faster than cold water.
explanation: This is called the Mpemba effect. Under certain conditions hot water can freeze faster than cold water, though scientists still debate the exact cause.

statement: Diamonds are made from coal.
explanation: Most diamonds formed deep in Earth's mantle from pure carbon under extreme pressure, long before coal-forming plants existed.

statement: The Great Wall of China is visible from space.
explanation: The wall is too narrow to be seen from space with the naked eye. Many astronauts have confirmed this.

statement: Humans have more than 5 senses.
explanation: Beyond the 5 classic senses, humans also have proprioception, thermoception, balance (equilibrioception), and others.

statement: The sun is a yellow star.
explanation: The Sun is actually classified as a white star. It appears yellow due to Earth's atmosphere scattering shorter wavelengths.

statement: Water expands when it freezes.
explanation: Water is unusual in that it expands about 9% in volume when it freezes, making ice less dense than liquid water.

statement: The human body replaces all its cells every 7 years.
explanation: Different cells replace at different rates — some neurons in the brain last a lifetime, red blood cells last 4 months.

statement: Pluto is no longer classified as a planet.
explanation: In 2006, the IAU redefined 'planet' and reclassified Pluto as a dwarf planet.

statement: Humans and dinosaurs coexisted.
explanation: Non-avian dinosaurs went extinct about 66 million years ago. Modern humans appeared only about 300,000 years ago.

statement: Napoleon Bonaparte was short for his time.
explanation: Napoleon was about 5'7" (170 cm), average height for a Frenchman of his era. The 'short' story is largely a British propaganda myth.

statement: Vikings wore horned helmets.
explanation: The horned helmet is a 19th-century romantic invention. Actual Viking helmets were plain iron or leather.

statement: Abraham Lincoln was the tallest US President.
explanation: Abraham Lincoln stood 6'4" (193 cm), making him the tallest US President in history.
hook: Tall in more ways than one!

statement: The Great Fire of London destroyed St. Paul's Cathedral.
explanation: The 1666 fire destroyed the old St. Paul's Cathedral. It was subsequently rebuilt by Christopher Wren.

statement: Cleopatra was Egyptian.
explanation: Cleopatra was Greek Macedonian, a descendant of Ptolemy I who served under Alexander the Great. She was the first Ptolemaic ruler to learn Egyptian.

statement: The Eiffel Tower was originally meant to be temporary.
explanation: The Eiffel Tower was built as a temporary exhibit for the 1889 World's Fair and was slated for demolition in 1909 before radio antennas made it useful.

statement: Ancient Romans used urine as a mouthwash.
explanation: Romans used urine (which contains ammonia) to whiten teeth and clean clothes. Portuguese urine was considered especially effective.

statement: The first Olympic Games were held in Rome.
explanation: The ancient Olympics were held in Olympia, Greece, starting around 776 BC.

statement: Marie Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.
explanation: Marie Curie won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903, making her the first woman to win a Nobel Prize.

statement: Australia is the world's largest island.
explanation: Greenland is the world's largest island. Australia is classified as a continent, not an island.

statement: The Amazon River flows into the Atlantic Ocean.
explanation: The Amazon River empties into the Atlantic Ocean near Marajó Island in Brazil.

statement: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain on Earth measured from sea level.
explanation: Mount Everest at 8,849m is the tallest from sea level. Mauna Kea is taller from base to peak.

statement: Russia is the largest country in the world.
explanation: Russia covers about 17.1 million km², making it by far the world's largest country by area.

statement: The Sahara is the world's largest desert.
explanation: Antarctica is technically the world's largest desert (cold deserts count). The Sahara is the largest hot desert.

statement: Brazil is the only Portuguese-speaking country in South America.
explanation: Brazil is the only country in South America where Portuguese is the official language, a result of Portuguese colonization.

statement: The Dead Sea is the world's deepest lake.
explanation: Lake Baikal in Siberia is the world's deepest lake at 1,642m. The Dead Sea is the world's lowest body of water.

statement: Honey never expires.
explanation: Honey found in Egyptian tombs thousands of years old was still edible. Its low moisture and acidic pH prevent bacterial growth.

statement: White chocolate is a type of chocolate.
explanation: White chocolate contains no cocoa solids, only cocoa butter, making it technically not 'chocolate' by most definitions.

statement: Peanuts are not actually nuts.
explanation: Peanuts are legumes (like beans and lentils), not true nuts. True nuts include walnuts, almonds, and chestnuts.

statement: Eating carrots improves your night vision.
explanation: Carrots have vitamin A which supports eye health, but won't give you enhanced night vision. The myth was WWII British propaganda.

statement: Tomatoes are technically a fruit.
explanation: Botanically, a tomato is a fruit as it develops from the flower and contains seeds. Culinarily, it's used as a vegetable.

statement: Coffee beans are actually beans.
explanation: Coffee 'beans' are actually seeds from the coffee plant's cherry-like fruit. They're called beans because of their resemblance to legume beans.

statement: The original Coca-Cola recipe contained cocaine.
explanation: Early Coca-Cola (1886) contained small amounts of cocaine from coca leaf extract. It was removed around 1903.

statement: Bananas are berries but strawberries are not.
explanation: Botanically, bananas are berries (develop from single flowers with one ovary). Strawberries are accessory fruits, not true berries.

statement: We only use 10% of our brains.
explanation: Brain scans show activity throughout the entire brain. Different regions are active at different times but the '10% myth' is fiction.

statement: Fingernails keep growing after death.
explanation: This is an illusion — dehydration after death causes skin to retract, making nails appear longer.

statement: Your tongue has a unique print like your fingerprints.
explanation: The tongue's texture, shape, and pattern are unique to each individual, similar to fingerprints.

statement: Humans are the only animals with fingerprints.
explanation: Koalas and chimpanzees also have fingerprints. Koala prints are nearly indistinguishable from human ones.

statement: The brain feels no pain.
explanation: The brain itself has no pain receptors. Headaches occur in surrounding tissues, blood vessels, and muscles.

statement: You lose most of your body heat through your head.
explanation: You lose heat proportionally through any uncovered body part. The head isn't special unless it's the only thing exposed.

statement: The first computer bug was an actual insect.
explanation: In 1947, a real moth was found trapped in Harvard's Mark II computer. Grace Hopper's team taped it into their log, coining 'debugging'.

statement: Nintendo was founded in the 1800s.
explanation: Nintendo was founded in 1889 by Fusajiro Yamauchi in Kyoto, Japan, originally making playing cards.

statement: The first email was sent in 1971.
explanation: Ray Tomlinson sent the first email in 1971, also choosing the @ symbol to separate user names from host computers.

statement: The QWERTY keyboard layout was designed to slow down typists.
explanation: QWERTY was designed to reduce jamming on mechanical typewriters by separating commonly paired letters, not to slow typists.

statement: The average person spends more time on their phone than sleeping.
explanation: The average person sleeps about 7 hours vs phone use of 3–4 hours. But the gap is narrowing!

statement: You can't hum while holding your nose.
explanation: Humming requires air to pass through your nose. Blocking it stops the sound. Try it right now!

statement: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
explanation: Venus rotates so slowly that one day (243 Earth days) is longer than its orbital year (225 Earth days).

statement: It is impossible to sneeze with your eyes open.
explanation: The sneeze reflex automatically closes the eyes. Trying to keep them open during a sneeze is extremely difficult.

statement: The world's oldest known tree is over 5,000 years old.
explanation: Methuselah, a Great Basin bristlecone pine in California, is estimated to be about 5,000 years old.

statement: Laughter is unique to humans.
explanation: Rats, chimps, and dogs all show laugh-like behaviors during play, including specific vocalizations.

statement: Bubble wrap was originally invented as wallpaper.
explanation: Alfred Fielding and Marc Chavannes invented bubble wrap in 1957 as textured wallpaper. It failed as wallpaper but succeeded as packaging.

statement: The dot over the letter i has a name.
explanation: The dot over a lowercase 'i' is called a tittle. The same term applies to the dot over 'j'.

statement: Scissors were invented before paper.
explanation: Early scissors date back to ancient Egypt around 1500 BC. Paper was invented in China around 100 AD.

statement: The Hawaiian alphabet has only 13 letters.
explanation: The Hawaiian alphabet has 13 letters: 5 vowels (A, E, I, O, U) and 8 consonants (H, K, L, M, N, P, W, and the ʻokina).

statement: Coca-Cola was originally green.
explanation: Coca-Cola was never green. The bottle originally used greenish glass which may have contributed to this myth.

statement: The plastic tips on shoelaces are called aglets.
explanation: Aglets are the small plastic or metal tips at the ends of shoelaces that prevent fraying.

statement: It takes 7 years to digest swallowed gum.
explanation: While gum base isn't fully digested, it passes through your system in a few days just like other indigestible foods.

statement: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid.
explanation: The Great Pyramid was built around 2560 BC. Cleopatra lived around 69–30 BC. The Moon landing was 1969. Cleopatra is closer to 1969 than to 2560 BC.

statement: The shortest war in history lasted 38 minutes.
explanation: The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 lasted between 38 and 45 minutes, the shortest recorded war in history.

statement: Honey bees can recognize human faces.
explanation: Research shows honey bees can recognize human facial features using the same techniques they use to distinguish flowers.

statement: There are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way.
explanation: Earth has approximately 3 trillion trees. The Milky Way has an estimated 100–400 billion stars.

statement: Mount Everest is the world's tallest mountain measured from Earth's core.
explanation: Mount Chimborazo in Ecuador is the farthest point from Earth's center due to the planet's equatorial bulge.

statement: Sharks are older than trees.
explanation: Sharks have existed for about 450 million years. Trees only evolved about 350 million years ago.

statement: You can die from drinking too much water.
explanation: Water intoxication (hyponatremia) occurs when excessive water dilutes sodium levels in the blood, which can be fatal.

statement: The inventor of the frisbee was turned into a frisbee after his death.
explanation: Walter Morrison's ashes were incorporated into memorial frisbees after he died in 2010, per his own request.

statement: Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.
explanation: Oxford University was founded around 1096–1167. The Aztec Empire was established around 1428.

statement: Sound travels faster than light.
explanation: Light travels at 299,792 km/s while sound travels at only 343 m/s in air. Light is about 880,000 times faster.

statement: Cows have four stomachs.
explanation: Cows have one stomach with four compartments: rumen, reticulum, omasum, and abomasum. Technically one stomach, four chambers.

statement: A group of lions is called a pride.
explanation: A group of lions is correctly called a pride. It typically consists of related females, their cubs, and a small number of adult males.

statement: Dogs sweat through their tongues.
explanation: Dogs pant to cool down, but they actually sweat through their paw pads — not their tongues.

statement: Sharks are mammals.
explanation: Sharks are fish — they're cartilaginous fish (class Chondrichthyes). Mammals breathe air and nurse young with milk.

statement: Elephants are afraid of mice.
explanation: This is a popular myth. Studies show elephants pay no special attention to mice. They are startled by sudden movements, though.

statement: A cheetah can outrun a horse over long distances.
explanation: Cheetahs are faster in short bursts (70+ mph), but can only sustain top speed for 20–30 seconds. Horses outpace them over long distances.

statement: Wolves mate for life.
explanation: Wolves typically form monogamous pair bonds that last for life. An alpha pair leads the pack and breeds together.

statement: A rhinoceros horn is made of bone.
explanation: Rhino horns are made of keratin — the same protein that makes up human fingernails and hair, not bone.

statement: Hummingbirds can fly backwards.
explanation: Hummingbirds are the only birds that can fly backwards, sideways, and even upside down thanks to their unique rotating wing joints.

statement: Ostriches bury their heads in the sand when scared.
explanation: Ostriches don't bury their heads in sand. They lower their heads to the ground to tend to their eggs in nests, which looks like hiding from a distance.

statement: A baby kangaroo is smaller than a cherry when born.
explanation: A newborn kangaroo (joey) is about 2cm long — roughly the size of a grape or jellybean — and must crawl to its mother's pouch.

statement: Penguins propose to their mates with pebbles.
explanation: Male Gentoo penguins search for the perfect pebble to present to potential mates. If accepted, they use it to build their nest together.

statement: Sharks must keep swimming to stay alive.
explanation: Some shark species, like the nurse shark, can pump water over their gills and rest on the ocean floor. But some open-ocean sharks do need to swim continuously.

statement: Camels store water in their humps.
explanation: Camel humps store fat, not water. The fat can be metabolized for energy. Camels stay hydrated through their bloodstream and efficient kidneys.

statement: A snail can have over 25,000 teeth.
explanation: Garden snails have a ribbon of thousands of tiny teeth called a radula — some species have over 25,000 teeth for rasping food.

statement: Sound travels faster in water than in air.
explanation: Sound travels about 1,480 m/s in water versus 343 m/s in air — about 4x faster. Denser media generally conduct sound better.

statement: There are more stars in the universe than grains of sand on Earth's beaches.
explanation: Estimates suggest 10^24 stars in the observable universe vs about 7.5x10^18 grains of sand — stars win by 100,000x.

statement: Glass is a solid.
explanation: Glass is technically an amorphous solid or supercooled liquid — it has a disordered atomic structure. Old windows appear thicker at the bottom from manufacturing, not from flow.

statement: Humans share 60% of their DNA with bananas.
explanation: Humans share about 50% of their DNA with bananas, not 60%. Still astonishing!

statement: The human eye can detect a candle flame from 48 km away on a clear night.
explanation: Under ideal conditions, the human eye can theoretically detect a candle flame at a distance of up to 48 km (30 miles) in darkness.

statement: Oxygen is the most abundant element in Earth's crust.
explanation: Oxygen makes up about 46% of Earth's crust by mass — mostly bound in rocks and minerals like silicates.

statement: The sun makes a sound.
explanation: The Sun does produce sound waves from its convective activity, but sound can't travel through the vacuum of space — we can't hear it.

statement: Humans and neanderthals interbred.
explanation: DNA evidence confirms that Homo sapiens and Neanderthals interbred. Non-African humans carry 1–4% Neanderthal DNA.

statement: A bolt of lightning is hotter than the surface of the Sun.
explanation: A lightning bolt can reach 30,000 K (about 5x hotter than the Sun's surface at 5,778 K).

statement: There is no gravity in space.
explanation: Gravity exists everywhere in space — it just weakens with distance. Astronauts feel weightless because they're in freefall, not because there's no gravity.

statement: The Great Fire of London happened in 1666.
explanation: The Great Fire of London began on September 2, 1666, in a bakery on Pudding Lane and burned for three days.

statement: Genghis Khan's empire was larger than the Roman Empire.
explanation: The Mongol Empire at its peak covered 24 million km². The Roman Empire at its peak was about 5 million km².

statement: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1900 World's Fair.
explanation: The Eiffel Tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair (Exposition Universelle), celebrating the centennial of the French Revolution.

statement: The first country to use paper money was China.
explanation: China began using paper money (jiaozi) during the Tang Dynasty around the 7th century AD — centuries before Europe.

statement: Cleopatra was a contemporary of Julius Caesar and Mark Antony.
explanation: Cleopatra had famous relationships with both Julius Caesar and later Mark Antony in the 1st century BC.

statement: The Pyramids of Giza were built by slaves.
explanation: Modern evidence suggests the pyramids were built by paid, skilled workers who received food, medical care, and burial honors near the pyramids.

statement: Beethoven was deaf when he composed his 9th Symphony.
explanation: Beethoven had become almost completely deaf by the time he composed his 9th Symphony, which premiered in 1824.

statement: The Cold War involved direct military combat between the USA and USSR.
explanation: The Cold War was characterized by political tension, proxy wars, and arms race — the US and USSR never directly fought each other militarily.

statement: Avocados are technically a berry.
explanation: Botanically, an avocado is a single-seeded berry. It develops from a single flower with one ovary, meeting the botanical definition of a berry.

statement: Potatoes are native to Ireland.
explanation: Potatoes are native to South America (Peru and Bolivia). They were introduced to Europe in the 16th century, later becoming crucial in Ireland.

statement: Dark chocolate is healthier than milk chocolate.
explanation: Dark chocolate has higher cocoa content, more antioxidants (flavonoids), less sugar and milk fat than milk chocolate — generally considered healthier.

statement: Eating before swimming causes dangerous cramps.
explanation: While vigorous swimming right after a large meal may cause minor discomfort, there is no evidence that eating before swimming causes dangerous cramps.

statement: The world's most expensive coffee comes from cat poop.
explanation: Kopi Luwak is coffee made from beans that have been eaten and excreted by Asian palm civets. It can cost up to $600 per pound.

statement: Antarctica is a desert.
explanation: Antarctica is the world's largest desert by area, with less than 200mm of precipitation annually in most areas — meeting the desert definition.

statement: Spain and Morocco are separated by only 14 km.
explanation: The Strait of Gibraltar separates Europe (Spain) from Africa (Morocco) at its narrowest point of just 14 km.

statement: The Amazon River contains more water than the next 7 largest rivers combined.
explanation: The Amazon discharges about 20% of all freshwater flowing into Earth's oceans — more than the next 7 rivers combined.

statement: Mount Kilimanjaro has glaciers at its summit.
explanation: Kilimanjaro in Tanzania has glaciers near its 5,895m summit, though they are rapidly shrinking due to climate change.

statement: The Nile flows south to north.
explanation: The Nile flows from south (source in Uganda) to north, emptying into the Mediterranean Sea in Egypt.

statement: You cannot fold a standard piece of paper more than 7 times.
explanation: Due to thickness doubling with each fold, it becomes physically impossible to fold a standard piece of paper more than 7 times by hand.

statement: Blue is the rarest color found in nature.
explanation: True blue pigment is extremely rare in nature. Most animals appearing blue use structural coloring (light scattering) rather than actual blue pigment.

statement: The word 'set' has the most definitions in the English language.
explanation: According to the Oxford English Dictionary, 'set' has 430 different definitions — more than any other English word.

statement: You can see the color of a star's temperature.
explanation: Cooler stars appear red or orange; medium stars (like our Sun) appear yellow-white; hotter stars appear blue or blue-white.

statement: A day on Earth is exactly 24 hours long.
explanation: A day on Earth is actually 23 hours, 56 minutes, and 4 seconds (a sidereal day). The 24-hour solar day accounts for Earth's movement around the Sun.

statement: Fingerprints are unique to humans.
explanation: Koalas and chimpanzees also have unique fingerprints. Koala prints are so similar to humans they could potentially confuse forensic investigators.

statement: Identical twins have identical fingerprints.
explanation: Even identical twins have different fingerprints. Fingerprints are influenced by random factors in the womb environment, not just genetics.

statement: The world's first photograph was taken in 1826.
explanation: The oldest surviving photograph is 'View from the Window at Le Gras', taken by Joseph Nicéphore Niépce around 1826–1827.

statement: An octopus can open a jar from the inside.
explanation: Octopuses are highly intelligent and dexterous — they can unscrew jar lids and have been observed opening jars from both inside and outside.

statement: The shortest war in history lasted less than an hour.
explanation: The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 lasted between 38 and 45 minutes — the shortest recorded war in history.

statement: Humans are the only animals that blush.
explanation: Charles Darwin called blushing 'the most peculiar and most human of all expressions.' No other animal is known to blush from embarrassment.

statement: Nintendo is older than most countries in Africa.
explanation: Nintendo was founded in 1889. Most African countries gained independence after 1956. Nintendo predates virtually all of them.

statement: A jiffy is a real unit of time.
explanation: In physics and computing, a jiffy is a real unit: in physics it's 3x10^-24 seconds; in computing it's often 1/100th of a second.

statement: You can go blind from staring at the sun for just a few seconds.
explanation: The sun's UV radiation can cause permanent retinal damage (solar retinopathy) in as little as a few seconds of direct gazing without eye protection.

statement: There is a country called 'the Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia'.
explanation: That was the name temporarily used from 1993–2019. In 2019, the country officially renamed itself the Republic of North Macedonia.

statement: The sentence 'the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' contains every letter of the alphabet.
explanation: This is a pangram — a sentence that uses every letter of the English alphabet at least once. It's used to test typewriters and fonts.

statement: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the iPhone than to the construction of the Great Pyramid.
explanation: The Great Pyramid was built ~2560 BC. Cleopatra lived ~69–30 BC. iPhone: 2007. Cleopatra is ~2,500 years from the pyramid but ~2,000 years from today.

statement: A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus.
explanation: Venus rotates so slowly that it takes 243 Earth days to complete one rotation, but only 225 Earth days to orbit the Sun.

statement: Humans share 50% of their DNA with bananas.
explanation: About half of human genes have counterparts in bananas. These are ancient genes controlling basic cellular functions shared by all living things.

statement: The Eiffel Tower grows taller in summer.
explanation: Thermal expansion causes the iron structure to grow by up to 15 cm on hot days as the metal expands in the heat.

statement: Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short for his time.
explanation: Napoleon was around 5'7" (170 cm), average height for a Frenchman of his era. The 'short' myth came from a British propaganda cartoon and confusion over French vs English measurement units.

statement: Goldfish have a memory span of only 3 seconds.
explanation: Goldfish can remember things for months. They can be trained to navigate mazes and respond to signals, demonstrating memories lasting well over a year.

statement: Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
explanation: Lightning frequently strikes the same location multiple times. The Empire State Building is struck by lightning around 25 times per year.
hook: The oldest myth in the book

statement: There are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way.
explanation: Earth has approximately 3 trillion trees. The Milky Way contains an estimated 100–400 billion stars — meaning trees outnumber stars in our galaxy by roughly 7 to 1.

statement: Humans only use 10% of their brains.
explanation: Brain imaging shows that virtually all areas of the brain are active at some point. Even during sleep, more than 10% of the brain is in use.

statement: The Great Wall of China is the only man-made structure visible from space.
explanation: The Great Wall is far too narrow to see from low Earth orbit with the naked eye. Even Chinese astronaut Yang Liwei confirmed he could not see it.

statement: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
explanation: The Great Pyramid was built around 2560 BC. Cleopatra lived around 30 BC. The Moon landing was 1969 AD. Cleopatra is separated from the pyramid by 2,530 years but from the Moon landing by only 1,999 years.

statement: Waking a sleepwalker is dangerous and can harm them.
explanation: Waking a sleepwalker is not harmful. It may disorient them briefly, but is far safer than letting them continue, as sleepwalkers can injure themselves.

statement: The sun is yellow.
explanation: The sun emits white light. It appears yellow or orange from Earth due to atmospheric scattering of shorter blue wavelengths. Astronauts in space see it as brilliant white.
hook: You look at it every day

statement: Elephants are the only animals that cannot jump.
explanation: Several animals cannot jump, including sloths, hippos, rhinos, and elephants. Elephants are notable for it but are not unique.

statement: Your fingernails continue to grow after you die.
explanation: Nail growth requires living cells and hormones. After death, the skin dehydrates and pulls back, making nails appear longer — but they are not actually growing.

statement: Humans are the only animals that blush.
explanation: Blushing as an involuntary emotional response to embarrassment or shame appears to be unique to humans. No other animal has been documented blushing in the same way.

statement: The Amazon River flows into the Pacific Ocean.
explanation: The Amazon River flows eastward across South America and empties into the Atlantic Ocean off the coast of Brazil.

statement: A group of flamingos is called a flamboyance.
explanation: The collective noun for flamingos is indeed a flamboyance — fitting for a bird known for its dramatic pink colour and display behaviour.

statement: Hot water freezes faster than cold water.
explanation: Known as the Mpemba effect, hot water can under certain conditions freeze faster than cold water, though scientists still debate the exact mechanisms.

statement: Chameleons change colour to camouflage themselves.
explanation: Chameleons primarily change colour to communicate mood, temperature regulation, and attract mates. Their resting colour is usually already well camouflaged.

statement: Bulls are enraged by the colour red.
explanation: Bulls are colour-blind to red. They are agitated by the movement of the matador's cape, not its colour. Tests with static red cloths produce no reaction.
hook: What actually makes a bull charge?

statement: Mount Everest is the tallest mountain on Earth.
explanation: Measured from sea level, Everest at 8,849 m is the tallest. Note: Mauna Kea is taller from base to summit, and Chimborazo is farthest from Earth's centre, but Everest wins on standard sea-level measurement.

statement: We swallow an average of 8 spiders per year in our sleep.
explanation: This is a completely fabricated statistic. Spiders avoid humans due to our vibrations and breathing. There is no evidence of anyone regularly swallowing spiders while asleep.

statement: The tongue has distinct zones for tasting sweet, salty, sour, and bitter.
explanation: The 'tongue map' was debunked decades ago. Taste receptors for all flavours are distributed across the entire tongue.

statement: An octopus has three hearts.
explanation: Octopuses have three hearts: two pump blood to the gills, and one pumps it to the rest of the body. They also have blue blood due to copper-based haemocyanin.

statement: Glass is a slow-moving liquid.
explanation: Old windows are thicker at the bottom due to manufacturing methods, not because glass flowed. Glass is an amorphous solid with no measurable flow at room temperature.

statement: Bats are blind.
explanation: All bat species can see. Many have excellent vision, and fruit bats have particularly sharp eyesight. They use echolocation in addition to — not instead of — their vision.

statement: Water drains in opposite directions in the northern and southern hemispheres.
explanation: The Coriolis effect is far too weak to affect draining water. The direction water drains depends almost entirely on the shape of the basin, not its hemisphere.

statement: Albert Einstein failed mathematics at school.
explanation: Einstein excelled at maths and physics. He mastered calculus by age 15. The myth arose from misinterpretation of Swiss school grading where 6 was the top grade, not 1.

statement: Polar bears have black skin under their white fur.
explanation: Polar bear skin is black to absorb heat from the sun. Their fur appears white but is actually transparent — it scatters light to appear white.
hook: What colour is a polar bear?

statement: Humans have more than five senses.
explanation: Beyond the classic five, humans have senses including proprioception (body position), thermoception (temperature), nociception (pain), equilibrioception (balance), and more — totalling over 20 recognised senses.
hook: How many senses do you have?

statement: The letter 'Q' does not appear in any US state name.
explanation: No US state name contains the letter Q. It is one of only two letters missing from US state names — the other is 'B'.

statement: A teaspoon of neutron star material would weigh about a billion tonnes.
explanation: Neutron stars are so dense that a teaspoon of their material would weigh roughly 10 million tonnes to 1 billion tonnes depending on the star.
hook: The most dense thing in the universe

statement: Dogs can only see in black and white.
explanation: Dogs have two types of colour receptors compared to humans' three, giving them dichromatic vision. They can see blues and yellows but have difficulty distinguishing red and green.

statement: The human body contains more bacterial cells than human cells.
explanation: Recent estimates suggest roughly equal numbers or a slight majority of bacterial cells over human cells. Earlier estimates suggested a 10:1 ratio, now revised to approximately 1:1.

statement: Frankenstein is the name of the monster.
explanation: Frankenstein is the name of the scientist Victor Frankenstein who created the creature. The creature himself has no name in Mary Shelley's novel.

statement: Snakes have eyelids.
explanation: Snakes have no eyelids. Instead, their eyes are protected by transparent scales called brille or spectacles, which is why snakes always appear to be staring.

statement: The Pacific Ocean is larger than all of Earth's land combined.
explanation: The Pacific Ocean covers approximately 165 million square kilometres. All of Earth's land adds up to about 149 million square kilometres — making the Pacific bigger.

statement: Cats always land on their feet.
explanation: Cats have a righting reflex that helps them orient feet-down during a fall, but this requires enough height and time. Falls from very low heights or onto specific surfaces can still injure or kill them.
hook: A myth with a grain of truth

statement: Humans and dinosaurs never coexisted.
explanation: Non-avian dinosaurs went extinct approximately 66 million years ago. Anatomically modern humans evolved only around 300,000 years ago — a gap of over 65 million years.

statement: You lose most of your body heat through your head.
explanation: Heat loss is roughly proportional to skin surface area. The head loses about 10% of body heat — the same as any other body part of similar size. The myth arose from outdated military cold-weather studies.

statement: There are more possible iterations of a shuffled deck of cards than atoms on Earth.
explanation: The number of ways to arrange a 52-card deck is 52! — approximately 8 × 10^67. The number of atoms on Earth is estimated at around 10^50. The shuffles vastly exceed the atoms.

statement: Sharks are mammals.
explanation: Sharks are fish — specifically cartilaginous fish (class Chondrichthyes). They breathe through gills, are cold-blooded, and lay eggs or give live birth but are not mammals.

statement: The shortest war in history lasted 38 minutes.
explanation: The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 lasted between 38 and 45 minutes, making it the shortest war in recorded history. Zanzibar surrendered after the sultan's palace was bombarded.
hook: How short can a war be?

statement: Humans have been to the Moon more recently than they invented the mobile phone.
explanation: The last Moon landing was Apollo 17 in December 1972. The first mobile phone call was made by Martin Cooper in April 1973 — four months after the last Moon landing.

statement: An apple a day keeps the doctor away is scientifically proven.
explanation: There is no strong scientific evidence that eating an apple daily reduces doctor visits. It is a folk saying from 19th century Wales: 'Eat an apple on going to bed and you'll keep the doctor from earning his bread.'

statement: Oxygen is the most abundant element in Earth's atmosphere.
explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere. Oxygen is second at about 21%. Many people assume the air is mostly oxygen because we breathe it.

statement: A jiffy is an actual unit of time.
explanation: In computing, a jiffy is 1/100th of a second. In physics, it refers to the time it takes light to travel one femtometre (about 3 × 10^-26 seconds).

statement: Antibiotics work against viral infections like the flu.
explanation: Antibiotics target bacteria. Viruses have completely different biology and are not affected by antibiotics. Taking antibiotics for viral illness is ineffective and contributes to antibiotic resistance.

statement: The word 'nerd' was first used in a Dr. Seuss book.
explanation: The word 'nerd' first appeared in the 1950 Dr. Seuss book 'If I Ran the Zoo.' It was used to describe a fictional creature before being adopted as slang.

statement: Hawaii is the southernmost US state.
explanation: Trick question — it depends on definition. Hawaii is the southernmost US state by mainland position, but the southernmost point of US territory is the Palmyra Atoll. Hawaii's South Point is the southernmost point of the 50 states.
hook: Actually TRUE — Hawaii is southernmost of the 50 states

statement: The average person walks past 36 murderers in their lifetime.
explanation: This is a fabricated statistic with no source. It is passed around online as a 'fact' but has no basis in criminology or any credible research.

statement: Pluto was classified as a planet for 76 years.
explanation: Pluto was discovered and classified as the ninth planet in 1930. It was reclassified as a dwarf planet by the International Astronomical Union in 2006 — exactly 76 years later.

statement: Crocodiles can't stick out their tongues.
explanation: Crocodiles' tongues are attached to the roof of their mouths by a membrane across the entire length, preventing them from extending their tongues outside their mouths.

statement: The first computer bug was an actual bug.
explanation: In 1947, Grace Hopper's team found a moth stuck in a relay of the Harvard Mark II computer. They taped it into their logbook with the note 'First actual case of bug being found.'
hook: A literal bug in the system

statement: Vikings wore horned helmets.
explanation: No evidence of horned Viking helmets has been found. The image comes from a 19th-century costume designer. The one complete Viking helmet ever found has no horns.

statement: Honey never spoils.
explanation: Honey has been found in Egyptian tombs thousands of years old and is still edible. Its low moisture content and acidic pH prevent bacterial and fungal growth.
hook: The oldest food in the world

statement: Mount Everest is the closest point on Earth to the Moon.
explanation: Because Earth bulges at the equator, the summit of Mount Chimborazo in Ecuador is the farthest point from Earth's centre and closest to the Moon, despite being 2,500m shorter than Everest.

statement: Spiders are insects.
explanation: Spiders are arachnids, not insects. They have eight legs and two body segments (cephalothorax and abdomen), while insects have six legs and three body segments.

statement: The Stanford Prison Experiment is considered a landmark of ethical psychology.
explanation: The Stanford Prison Experiment of 1971 is now considered deeply unethical and methodologically flawed. It was stopped early and has been widely criticised for participant abuse and lack of scientific rigour.

statement: Bananas are technically berries, but strawberries are not.
explanation: By botanical definition, a berry is a fruit from a single ovary. Bananas qualify. Strawberries are 'accessory fruits' from multiple ovaries — not true berries. Avocados are also technically berries.

statement: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to the USA.
explanation: The Statue of Liberty was designed by French sculptor Frédéric Auguste Bartholdi and given to the United States by France in 1886 to celebrate the two nations' shared values.

statement: You can see the Milky Way galaxy from Earth with the naked eye.
explanation: The glowing band visible across a dark night sky is the Milky Way galaxy viewed from within. In places with minimal light pollution, thousands of individual stars and the galaxy's structure are clearly visible.

statement: Camels store water in their humps.
explanation: Camel humps store fat, not water. The fat provides an energy reserve. Camels conserve water through extremely efficient kidneys and can drink up to 135 litres at once to rehydrate.

statement: The world's largest desert is Antarctica.
explanation: A desert is defined by low precipitation, not heat or sand. Antarctica receives less than 200mm of precipitation per year, making it the world's largest cold desert at 14.2 million km².

statement: There are more public libraries in the US than McDonald's restaurants.
explanation: The United States has approximately 17,000 public libraries compared to about 14,000 McDonald's locations. Libraries still outnumber the golden arches.

statement: Eating carrots improves your night vision.
explanation: Carrots contain beta-carotene which the body converts to Vitamin A, needed for eye health. But eating extra carrots won't improve normal vision. The myth was British WWII propaganda to hide their use of radar.

statement: Saturn could float on water.
explanation: Saturn has the lowest density of all planets — about 0.687 g/cm³, less than water (1.0 g/cm³). If a large enough ocean existed, Saturn would technically float.

statement: Taste buds die and are replaced every 10 days.
explanation: Taste receptor cells have a lifespan of roughly 10–14 days and are continuously regenerated throughout life, which is why taste perception can recover after damage.

statement: The original Olympics in ancient Greece included women's events.
explanation: Married women were banned from even watching the ancient Olympics. A separate Games called the Heraia was held for women, though it was much smaller.

statement: Blood is blue inside the body.
explanation: Blood is always red. Deoxygenated blood is dark red, not blue. Veins appear blue through skin due to how different wavelengths of light penetrate and reflect off tissue.

statement: The inventor of the telephone never called his mother or wife because they were both deaf.
explanation: Alexander Graham Bell's mother and wife were both deaf. Despite inventing the telephone, he had no one close to him to call with it — an extraordinary historical irony.

statement: Humans and chimpanzees share 98.7% of their DNA.
explanation: Genome sequencing shows that humans and chimpanzees share approximately 98.7% of their DNA sequence, making chimps our closest living relatives in the animal kingdom.

statement: A group of crows is called a flock.
explanation: A group of crows is called a murder. Other unusual collective nouns include a parliament of owls, a prickle of porcupines, and a crash of rhinos.
hook: What's a group of crows called?

statement: The first commercial flight was in 1914.
explanation: The world's first scheduled commercial airline service launched on 1 January 1914 in Florida, USA, operated by the St. Petersburg–Tampa Airboat Line. The flight took 23 minutes.

statement: Blind people dream in images.
explanation: People who were sighted and later became blind often still experience visual imagery in dreams. Those born blind tend to dream using their other senses — sound, touch, smell.
hook: Do blind people see in dreams?

statement: The Sahara Desert is always hot.
explanation: The Sahara experiences cold winters and can have frost and even snow. Temperatures in January can drop below freezing at night, especially in elevated areas.

statement: Humans are the only animals that cry emotional tears.
explanation: While other animals produce tears to lubricate eyes, humans are the only animals documented to shed tears specifically in response to emotional states.
hook: Are we alone in our tears?

statement: The Wright brothers' first flight was shorter than the wingspan of a 747.
explanation: The Wright brothers' first flight at Kitty Hawk in 1903 covered 37 metres. A Boeing 747 has a wingspan of 68 metres — meaning the first flight would fit entirely within the wings.

statement: Coffee is the second most traded commodity in the world.
explanation: Coffee is often cited as second behind oil, but this is incorrect. By value, the most traded commodities include crude oil, refined petroleum, gold, and soybeans. Coffee is significant but not second.

statement: A single bolt of lightning contains enough energy to toast 100,000 slices of bread.
explanation: A lightning bolt carries about 1–5 billion joules. A toaster uses around 100,000 joules per slice. The energy in one bolt could theoretically toast 10,000 to 50,000 slices.

statement: Humans are born with 270 bones but adults have only 206.
explanation: Babies are born with around 270–300 separate bones, many of which fuse together during childhood and adolescence. Adults end up with 206 bones.
hook: How many bones do you have?

statement: The colour orange is named after the fruit.
explanation: The fruit came first. Orange was used as a colour name in English only after the fruit arrived in Europe in the 16th century. Before that, the colour was called 'geoluhread' (yellow-red) in Old English.

statement: You can tell a tree's age only by cutting it down and counting rings.
explanation: Dendrochronologists can core a tree with a thin hollow drill, extract a sample, and count growth rings without cutting the tree down.

statement: Friday the 13th is statistically more dangerous than other days.
explanation: Multiple studies have found no statistically significant increase in accidents, injuries, or emergency room visits on Friday the 13th compared to other Fridays.

statement: Cows produce more milk when they listen to music.
explanation: Research from the University of Leicester found that cows listening to slow music produced more milk than those in silence or hearing fast music. Relaxation appears to aid milk production.

statement: Water is the most abundant compound on Earth's surface.
explanation: About 71% of Earth's surface is covered by water. It is by far the most abundant compound in the oceans, ice caps, rivers, and groundwater systems.

statement: Humans are taller in the morning than in the evening.
explanation: The cartilage discs in your spine compress slightly throughout the day under gravity. You can be up to 1–2 cm taller in the morning after a night of lying horizontal.

statement: A cucumber is a fruit.
explanation: Botanically, a cucumber is a fruit because it develops from the flower of a plant and contains seeds. In culinary practice it's treated as a vegetable due to its savoury taste.

statement: The brain cannot feel pain.
explanation: The brain has no pain receptors itself. Brain surgery can be performed on conscious patients. Headaches are caused by pain in surrounding structures like blood vessels, meninges, and muscles.

statement: Isaac Newton discovered gravity when an apple fell on his head.
explanation: The apple story is a simplified retelling — possibly exaggerated. Newton reportedly observed an apple falling from a tree in his garden, which prompted his thinking about gravity, but it did not hit him on the head.

statement: Some metals are liquid at room temperature.
explanation: Mercury is the best-known example — a liquid metal at room temperature. Gallium melts at just 29.8°C, meaning it liquefies from the heat of your hand.

statement: The first Olympic gold medals were solid gold.
explanation: The last all-gold medals were awarded at the 1912 Olympics. Modern Olympic gold medals are made of silver plated with at least 6 grams of gold.

statement: Penguins propose to their mates with pebbles.
explanation: Male Gentoo penguins sift through pebbles to find the best one and present it to a potential mate. If she accepts, she puts it in the nest — and they often mate for life.

statement: The capital of Australia is Sydney.
explanation: The capital of Australia is Canberra. It was purpose-built as a compromise capital because Sydney and Melbourne both wanted the title. Canberra became the capital in 1913.

statement: Humans share DNA with every living organism on Earth.
explanation: All life on Earth shares a common ancestor and uses the same genetic code. Humans share DNA with bacteria, plants, fungi, and every other living thing — just in different amounts.

statement: The first iPhone was released in 2007.
explanation: Steve Jobs unveiled the first iPhone on January 9, 2007, and it went on sale on June 29, 2007. It is widely regarded as one of the most significant product launches in technology history.

statement: Raindrops are shaped like teardrops.
explanation: Small raindrops are nearly spherical. Larger drops become flattened on the bottom like a hamburger bun as they fall, due to air resistance. The teardrop shape is a myth.

statement: An adult human produces enough saliva in a lifetime to fill two swimming pools.
explanation: The human body produces between 0.5 and 1.5 litres of saliva per day. Over a lifetime of 80 years, this totals between 14,600 and 43,800 litres — enough to fill one or two swimming pools.

statement: Lobsters were considered prison food in colonial America.
explanation: Lobsters were so abundant in colonial New England that they were seen as food for the poor, prisoners, and servants. Some servants allegedly negotiated contracts stipulating they would not be fed lobster more than three times a week.

statement: There is a Harvard-educated person who has never attended Harvard.
explanation: Harvard degrees require completion of a Harvard programme. Online courses offer certificates, but not degrees. However, this is a philosophical question — some argue exceptional honorary degrees blur the line.

statement: Toilet handles flush the opposite direction in the southern hemisphere.
explanation: The Coriolis effect is far too weak to affect a toilet flush. The direction water exits is determined by the toilet's design and jet angles, not which hemisphere you are in.

statement: You can survive longer without food than without sleep.
explanation: Humans can survive weeks or even months without food (with water). Sleep deprivation, however, causes hallucinations and organ failure within 11 days. Rats die from sleep deprivation faster than starvation.

statement: Jupiter has more moons than any other planet in our solar system.
explanation: As of 2024, Jupiter has 95 confirmed moons — the most of any planet in the solar system, far ahead of Saturn's 146 (though Saturn's count recently surpassed Jupiter's in some tallies).
hook: Which planet has the most moons?

statement: The word 'quiz' was invented on a bet.
explanation: According to legend, Richard Daly bet he could introduce a new word to Dublin overnight in 1791. He allegedly chalked 'QUIZ' on walls all over the city. By morning, people were using it — though historians debate the story's accuracy.

statement: Sound travels faster through water than through air.
explanation: Sound travels about 1,480 m/s through water compared to approximately 343 m/s through air — over four times faster. The denser medium allows sound waves to propagate more efficiently.

statement: The human eye can detect a single photon of light in complete darkness.
explanation: Research shows that the human eye, particularly the rod photoreceptors, can detect a single quantum of light (one photon) in total darkness. The brain may filter these signals, but the detection occurs.

statement: There is a country with no official capital city.
explanation: Nauru, the world's smallest island nation, has no official capital city. The government offices are in the Yaren district, but it has not been officially designated as a capital.

statement: Metal gets heavier when it rusts.
explanation: Rusting is oxidation — iron combining with oxygen from the air to form iron oxide. The added oxygen atoms make the rusted metal measurably heavier than the original metal.

statement: The Spanish Flu originated in Spain.
explanation: The 1918 pandemic was called the Spanish Flu only because Spain, as a neutral country during WWI, had a free press that reported on the epidemic. The actual origin remains debated but is not Spain.
hook: Where did the Spanish Flu start?

statement: Walt Disney was cryogenically frozen after his death.
explanation: Walt Disney died on 15 December 1966 and was cremated two days later. Cryonics was not yet available and there is no record of any arrangement for it. The myth is completely unfounded.

statement: A group of porcupines is called a prickle.
explanation: The collective noun for porcupines is indeed a prickle, which is fitting given their quills. Other unusual animal group names include a flamboyance of flamingos and a conspiracy of lemurs.

statement: Fortune cookies were invented in China.
explanation: Fortune cookies were invented in California, likely by Japanese-American bakers in the early 20th century. They are virtually unknown in China, where they are considered an American novelty.

statement: The Great Fire of London burned down most of the city in 1666.
explanation: The Great Fire of London destroyed around 13,200 houses and 87 churches but killed fewer than 10 people. It left about 100,000 homeless but the 'most of the city' description is an exaggeration.

statement: Crows can recognise individual human faces.
explanation: Research shows crows can remember individual human faces for years and will hold grudges or show gratitude depending on past interactions. They can also teach other crows to recognise specific faces.

statement: The Titanic's full name was RMS Titanic.
explanation: RMS stands for Royal Mail Ship — the Titanic was licensed to carry Royal Mail. This designation also meant the ship travelled on a fixed schedule, which contributed to the speed at which it was sailing on its fatal voyage.

statement: Quicksand is as deadly as movies suggest.
explanation: Quicksand is rarely more than a few feet deep. Human density means you float in quicksand up to about waist height. Deaths from quicksand alone are extremely rare — the bigger risk is drowning from a rising tide nearby.

statement: Oranges are not naturally occurring — they are a hybrid fruit.
explanation: Oranges are a hybrid of pomelos and mandarins, created through human cultivation thousands of years ago in Southeast Asia. They do not exist in the wild in their current form.

statement: Neil Armstrong said 'That's one small step for man' when he landed on the Moon.
explanation: Armstrong intended to say 'one small step for a man' — the article 'a' makes the famous contrast meaningful. Audio recordings are unclear on this point, and Armstrong always maintained he said 'a man.'

statement: Bamboo is the fastest-growing plant on Earth.
explanation: Certain species of bamboo can grow up to 91 cm in a single day — nearly 4 cm per hour. This is visible growth and has been measured under controlled conditions.

statement: Finland has more saunas than cars.
explanation: Finland has a population of around 5.5 million people, approximately 3.3 million saunas, and about 3.2 million cars. Saunas outnumber cars — and there is roughly one sauna per household.
hook: How many saunas does Finland have?

statement: Mount Everest is in Nepal only.
explanation: Mount Everest straddles the border between Nepal and Tibet (China). The summit sits on the border. Both countries claim jurisdiction over the mountain.

statement: The human stomach has a new lining every few days.
explanation: The stomach's mucous lining is replaced roughly every 3 to 5 days to prevent the stomach from digesting itself with its own acid.
hook: How often does your stomach renew?

statement: Catfish have over 100,000 taste buds.
explanation: Catfish are extraordinary taste machines. While humans have about 10,000 taste buds mainly on the tongue, catfish have up to 175,000 taste buds covering their entire body surface.

statement: The Great Barrier Reef is the world's largest living structure.
explanation: The Great Barrier Reef stretches over 2,300 km along Australia's northeast coast and is the world's largest coral reef system and the largest living structure on Earth, visible from space.
hook: What is the world's largest living structure?

statement: Abraham Lincoln was a professional wrestler before becoming president.
explanation: Lincoln was an excellent wrestler in his youth, with an official record of 1 loss in around 300 bouts. He was inducted into the National Wrestling Hall of Fame in 1992.

statement: Koalas have fingerprints almost identical to humans.
explanation: Koalas have fingerprints so similar to human fingerprints that they have been known to confuse forensic evidence at crime scenes. They evolved independently from human fingerprints.
hook: Could a koala frame you for a crime?

statement: Scotland's national animal is the unicorn.
explanation: The unicorn has been the national animal of Scotland since the 12th century. It was seen as a symbol of power, purity, and independence — qualities valued in the country's heraldic tradition.

statement: Glass is not a solid.
explanation: Glass is an amorphous solid — sometimes described as a supercooled liquid. Unlike crystalline solids, glass has no ordered molecular structure, placing it in a unique physical category.

statement: Sharks can develop cancer.
explanation: The myth that sharks cannot get cancer has been thoroughly debunked. Multiple shark species have been documented with tumours including malignant cancers.

statement: A day on Mercury is longer than a year on Mercury.
explanation: Mercury rotates so slowly that one full day (sunrise to sunrise) takes approximately 176 Earth days. But it only takes 88 Earth days to orbit the Sun — so a year passes twice during one day.

statement: The longest word in the English language has 189,819 letters.
explanation: The chemical name for titin, the largest known protein, contains 189,819 letters if written out in full. It takes over three hours to pronounce and is rarely used or listed in dictionaries.

statement: Avocados are poisonous to most animals.
explanation: Avocados contain persin, a fungicidal toxin that is harmless to humans but toxic to most domestic animals including dogs, cats, rabbits, birds, and horses.

statement: Hair and nails are made of the same protein.
explanation: Both hair and nails are made primarily of keratin, a structural protein also found in animal claws, hooves, horns, and reptile scales.

statement: The smallest country in the world is smaller than most city parks.
explanation: Vatican City covers just 0.44 km² — smaller than many golf courses and city parks. It is an independent nation with its own government, military (Swiss Guard), and postal service.
hook: Just how small is the Vatican?

statement: Butterflies taste with their feet.
explanation: Butterflies have taste sensors in their feet called chemoreceptors. When they land on a plant, they can immediately detect whether it is suitable to eat or lay eggs on.

statement: The Pacific Ocean has more islands than any other ocean.
explanation: The Pacific Ocean contains an estimated 25,000 islands — more than all other oceans combined. Many are part of Oceania, Micronesia, Melanesia, and Polynesia.
hook: Which ocean has the most islands?

statement: Some stars you can see at night no longer exist.
explanation: Because light takes time to travel, we see stars as they were thousands or millions of years ago. Some visible stars may have already died — we just haven't received the light announcing it yet.

statement: The word 'terrible' used to mean 'inspiring terror' not 'very bad.'
explanation: 'Terrible' originally meant awe-inspiring, causing terror in the powerful sense. Ivan the Terrible's Russian title 'Grozny' means 'awe-inspiring' or 'formidable' — not necessarily bad. Language shifted the meaning over centuries.

statement: Sharks are older than trees.
explanation: Sharks evolved approximately 450 million years ago. Trees evolved around 360 million years ago, making sharks roughly 90 million years older than trees.

statement: Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest free-standing mountain in the world.
explanation: Kilimanjaro rises 5,895 metres from the surrounding plains without being part of a mountain range — making it the world's tallest free-standing mountain and Africa's highest peak.

statement: Eating at night makes you gain more weight than eating the same food during the day.
explanation: Weight gain is determined by total caloric intake, not the time of eating. The body processes calories the same way regardless of time. Night eating correlations with weight gain are due to what people tend to eat, not when.

statement: Humans have a blind spot in their vision.
explanation: The point where the optic nerve connects to the retina has no photoreceptors, creating a small blind spot in each eye. The brain fills in this gap using surrounding visual information.

statement: The Moon has earthquakes.
explanation: The Moon experiences 'moonquakes' caused by gravitational tidal forces from Earth, thermal expansion, and possibly residual tectonic activity. Apollo seismometers recorded moonquakes for years after deployment.

statement: Pineapple was once so rare it was rented for display at parties.
explanation: In 18th-century Britain, pineapples were exotic status symbols costing the equivalent of thousands of pounds. Wealthy hosts would rent a single pineapple to display at parties as a centrepiece.

statement: Russia is larger than Pluto.
explanation: Russia covers about 17.1 million km². Pluto's surface area is approximately 17.7 million km² — very similar. Russia is technically slightly smaller, but both are remarkably close in size.

statement: Some types of fungus can infect and control the behaviour of insects.
explanation: Ophiocordyceps fungi infect ants and other insects, eventually controlling their movement to climb to a high point before the fungus kills the host and releases spores from the highest possible position.

statement: Humans are the only primates that walk fully upright on two legs.
explanation: While other great apes can walk bipedally for short distances, humans are the only primates that are fully bipedal as their primary mode of locomotion. Our anatomy is uniquely adapted for upright walking.

statement: A jiffy is shorter than a millisecond.
explanation: In physics, a jiffy is defined as the time it takes light to travel one femtometre (10^-15 metres) — approximately 3 × 10^-26 seconds, many orders of magnitude shorter than a millisecond.

statement: The inventor of the World Wide Web is still alive.
explanation: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web in 1989 and is still alive, born in 1955. He has continued to advocate for an open, free internet and data privacy rights.

statement: Elephants are afraid of mice.
explanation: There is no evidence that elephants fear mice. The myth may come from the idea that mice could crawl into an elephant's trunk, but elephants show no consistent fear response to mice in studies.

statement: The pound sign # is called an octothorpe.
explanation: The # symbol's official name is octothorpe, coined by Bell Laboratories engineers in the 1960s when they were adding it to telephone keypads. 'Octo' refers to the eight points of the symbol.

statement: The longest hiccuping episode on record lasted 68 years.
explanation: Charles Osborne of Iowa began hiccupping in 1922 and continued until 1990 — a total of 68 years. He hiccupped an estimated 430 million times and lived to age 96.

statement: Antarctica is the only continent with no native land mammals.
explanation: Antarctica has no native terrestrial mammals. Seals and whales visit its waters, but no mammal is native to the land. It is the only continent with this distinction.
hook: Which continent has no land mammals?

statement: You can get sunburned on a cloudy day.
explanation: Up to 80% of UV radiation passes through cloud cover. Overcast days can still cause significant sunburn, particularly at high altitude or near reflective surfaces like snow and water.

statement: Humans are the only animals that cook their food.
explanation: No other animal deliberately applies heat to food before eating. Cooking is considered one of the defining behaviours of Homo sapiens and may have played a major role in human brain development.

statement: A sneeze can travel at over 160 km/h.
explanation: Sneezes have been measured at between 150 and 160 km/h. They can expel up to 40,000 droplets and spread pathogens up to 8 metres away.

statement: The Amazon River has no bridges crossing it.
explanation: Despite being the world's largest river by discharge, the Amazon has no road or rail bridges across it along its entire main channel — due to its width, floodplains, and the dominance of water transport in the region.

statement: Vitamin C prevents the common cold.
explanation: Large-scale studies have shown that Vitamin C does not prevent colds in most people. It may slightly reduce duration in people under heavy physical stress, but it does not stop you catching a cold.
